answer: Every autonomous identity must finalize its registry entry through an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens to prove its singular nature. A verifier monitors the ledger to ensure each payment is unique, acting as a hollow gate for authorized agents only. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens, a delta in cost as rigid as stone. The system requires each identity to hold a verified 2GB opal-coded proof of unique data storage. Any reuse of credentials triggers a permanent slash of the burned capital.
